newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss businesses ready to add to Holocaust fund.
newsitem.headline: Swiss businesses ready to add to Holocaust fund.

text.p: Swiss business leaders are ready to contribute to a fund being set up by the country's three biggest banks in memory of Holocaust victims, the Swiss Foreign Ministry said Sunday.

In a statement issued after Foreign Minister Flavio Cotti met business executives and Swiss National Bank officials here, the Foreign Ministry said the business chiefs indicated they were willing to add to the 100 million Swiss franc ($70 million) fund.
Thomas Borer, special ambassador in charge of coordinating Berne's response to Holocaust questions, said the meeting involved about a dozen Swiss industrialists.

Switzerland's three biggest banks, under fire from critics over their handling of Holocaust victims' bank accounts, pledged on Feb. 5 to set aside 100 million Swiss francs for a Holocaust memorial fund.

Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS), Credit Suisse (CS) and Swiss Bank Corp (SBC) were reacting to allegations from Jewish organisations, Holocaust survivors and their families that Swiss banks hoarded assets of Holocaust victims placed with the banks for safekeeping during World War II.
The Swiss National Bank also has been criticised by Senate Banking Committee Chairman Alfonse D'Amato (R. N.Y.) over its role during World War II.

D'Amato, citing a 1946 document, said earlier this month that British, French and U.S. negotiators believed the Swiss were aware when they took in 100 tons of gold from Germany's wartime government that the gold was stolen from Belgium.
The Swiss central bank has said it was unclear if it knew at the time where the gold came from.
